key_bets: Q>1 achievable in an electrostatic confinement device — the entire economic case is conditional on a physics result not yet demonstrated
Coulomb collision losses can be mitigated through electron co-confinement geometry (Lampe-Mannheimer 1998 cited 25-37× faster than fusion for this device class)
Space-charge limit can be exceeded by ~50× via electron co-confinement (currently supported by PIC simulations only, not experimentally demonstrated)
Modular mass-manufacturing of small (1-100 kWe) Orbitron units stacks economically to commercial plant scale despite undefined plant architecture
Sustained 300 kV HV feedthrough operates reliably under cumulative 14 MeV neutron bombardment over commercial timescales
Thermal-cycle energy conversion is achievable at module scale despite turbines being impractical below ~1 MWe
Purchased tritium supply at >$35,000/g remains economically viable indefinitely without a breeding blanket
eliminated_costs: Large superconducting magnets — only a small 0.5 T HTS coil pair required, eliminating the dominant tokamak CAPEX driver (~30-40% of tokamak CAPEX)
Tritium breeding blanket — no FLiBe or LiPb blanket needed, eliminating ~15-25% of tokamak CAPEX (replaced by purchased tritium as OPEX)
Conventional plasma heating systems (RF, NBI) — replaced by HV power supply and ion gun array
Large REBCO tape supply chain dependency — coil dimensions are too small to be constrained by global REBCO production capacity
Beryllium and FLiBe material supply chains — not required at any scale
novel_costs: Sustained 300 kV high-voltage power supply and proprietary HV feedthroughs — a CAPEX category with no analogue in tokamak TEA
Permanent purchased tritium OPEX at >$35,000/g with no breeding offset — scales inversely with Q and could add $0.01-0.10/kWh
Per-module neutron shielding ("concrete castle" per device) for stacked-module arrays — economically self-defeating at small scale without redesign
Cathode replacement under combined 14 MeV neutron and ion bombardment — primary variable O&M driver with no lifetime data
Module-scale energy conversion (thermoelectric ~5-15% efficiency) — entirely novel cost category since turbines don't work at 1-100 kWe

risks.description: Q>1 not demonstrated in any electrostatic confinement device — the entire economic case is conditional on an unproven physics result
Coulomb collision losses unretired — Lampe-Mannheimer 1998 analysis cites collision rate 25-37× faster than fusion; Avalanche's response is theoretical, not experimentally validated
Space-charge mitigation via electron co-confinement is supported by PIC simulations only; AIP Advances 2024 paper states demonstration is "the focus of initial experiments"
Energy conversion at 1-100 kWe module scale is undefined — turbines impractical below ~1 MWe and no alternative pathway has been engineered
No commercial plant architecture exists — module count, BOP layout, multi-module shielding, and tritium handling at fleet scale all undefined
No tritium breeding blanket design — FFC MoU is a collaboration direction with no specification or timeline; tritium cost could dominate LCOE at low Q
Overnight capital cost per kWe is unbounded — only public figure is aspirational <$1B total with no cost basis
Cathode and HV feedthrough lifetime under sustained 14 MeV neutron bombardment is uncharacterized with no fission analogue
Diocotron and electron cyclotron drift instabilities flagged in PIC simulations but uncharacterized experimentally
Per-module neutron shielding requirements (concrete castle) may make modular architecture economically self-defeating without integrated redesign
O&M cost structure entirely uncharacterized — placeholder 3-5% CAPEX/yr fixed and $5-15/MWh variable have no Orbitron-specific anchor
Ion-cathode impact risk at 300 kV requires precise orbit stability not yet demonstrated at fusion-relevant conditions (Talk-Polywell critique)
Scaling from demonstrated 100 kV to 300 kV operating point not publicly characterized (Physics of Plasmas 2025 paper accessible only as abstract)
HTS magnet upgrade from 0.05 T permanent magnets to 0.5 T superconducting design is a technology development step, not procurement
Limited public technical disclosure — peer-reviewed papers paywalled with only abstracts available, no independent TEA or plant study published
